title: Study of Bioinsecticidal Activity of Water-Soluble Linalool Derivative
content: Plant-derived compounds are increasingly being investigated as potential alternatives or supplements to conventional insecticides. This study evaluated the insecticidal activity of linalool and its ester derivative against adults of Eurygaster integriceps and Eurygaster maura, two important pests of cereal crops. Llinalool monomethyl succinate derivative were synthesized, and their formation was assessed using thin-layer chromatography and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy. Linalool, formulated as an aqueous emulsion, and linalyl monomethyl succinate, formulated as an aqueous alcoholic solution, were selected for laboratory bioassays. Their insecticidal activity was evaluated at concentrations of 1%, 5%, 10%, and 20%, with a 0% vehicle control, following topical application. Both formulations caused concentration-dependent mortality and reduced locomotor activity in the tested insects. At a concentration of 20%, the linalool emulsion caused 100% mortality in both species within 24 h, while linalyl monomethyl succinate produced 90% mortality within 72 h under the reported experimental conditions. These findings indicate that linalool and linalyl monomethyl succinate are promising candidates for further investigation as insecticidal agents against E. integriceps and E. maura. Additional field studies and assessments of their environmental fate and non-target effects are required before their potential application in integrated pest management can be established.
